text: by the knowledge arisen from hearing [he sees] thus: in the realm of animals there are animals, thoroughly afflicted, who live on the food of joy: in the forest thickets the great serpent called Ājagara, which lives eating the food of joy and wind, and the creature Golgolika, and those called "dwellers on the mountain slopes," and others besides. Among these, the food of joy of the gods of Clear Light is a living by the food of joy free of malice, but the food of joy of animals is accompanied by views of enmity and a mind that holds enmity firmly. Thinking, "By which of these is one born there?", when he examines with the knowledge arisen from hearing, [he sees that] whoever is predominantly hateful or of a hateful nature, in keeping with the cause of enmity, and predominantly deluded, if he takes life, then on parting from the body he falls wrongly into the bad destinies and is born among the hell beings. If one who has that basis of enmity and joy is born among animals, he comes to eat the food of joy and wind. If he is born as a human, of equal fortune with humans, then, in keeping with the cause of that deed, he is seen always to become involved suddenly in fighting with others without cause. Then again that monk who knows the ripening of the fruits of deeds examines the boundless world of animals in another way. Thinking, "How again are those that move in the water born?", when he examines with the knowledge arisen from hearing, [he sees that] whoever, of weak intellect and weak consciousness, dies while tormented by thirst, on parting from the body falls wrongly into the bad destinies and becomes one that moves in the water
